newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana expects some 10 company listings in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Botswana expects some 10 company listings in 1997.

text.p: At least 10 foreign companies are expected to list on the Botswana Stock Exchange this year, exchange chairman Louis Nchindo said on Friday.

"No fewer than 10 companies with primary stock exchange listings in Ireland, Canada, Australia and of course South Africa, will have dual listing on the BSE or have declared their intention to do so," he said.
Nchindo was speaking at the listing on the BSE of diamond giant De Beers Consolidated Mines/Centenary linked units and Regent Undervalued Assets Africa Fund, a firm geared to investment in Africa.

The listing of De Beers, which opened at 125 pula giving the firm a market capitalisation of 38.4 billion pula, boosted the BSE's market capitalisation 50 times. Regent debuted at 38 pula. Nchindo said since the inauguration of the BSE in 1995 management had worked towards increasing investor access to the underlying economy of Botswana and to promote cross-border investment.
"We identified the dual listings as a means to widen investment opportunities for individuals, corporations and institutional investors such as life assurance and pension funds," he said.
Nchindo said the BSE would from Friday introduce two new indices, namely the Foreign Companies Index and the All Companies Index.
During a pre-listing dinner on Thursday De Beers chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said the Botswana listing would boost trade and investment between Botswana and its southern African neighbours.
De Beers, which has operations in South Africa and Namibia, is an equal partner with the Botswana government in Debswana which operates the country's three diamond mines.
Ranked by value Botswana is the largest diamond producing country in the world. Its entire diamond production is sold though the London-based and De Beers' controlled Central Selling Organisation.
Regent, which is keen on involvement in mining opportunities in Africa, is seeking to raise $50 million. It has said it will invest some 2.5 percent of this in Botswana.
